                        </ns0:gap>ish.</ns0:hi> T<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s signifieth the di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ference o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Professors,</ns0:hi> some have <ns0:hi>Lamps,</ns0:hi> make a Profe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sio<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, but have no Truth of Grace, others have the root of the m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tter in them, a true <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> which feeds Me<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s Profession. The <ns0:hi>Bridegrooms</ns0:hi> tarrying, sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ts delaying to come to Judgment, their <ns0:hi>Slumbring</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sleeping</ns0:hi> signifies the Infirmities of the best, who Sleep, tho their Hearts Wake; and the deeper se<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>urity of others in the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r sinful state. The <ns0:hi>coming of</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Bridegroom at Mid-night.</ns0:hi> Sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth Christ's coming, in a dark time of <ns0:hi>Troubles</ns0:hi> and Afflictions, or at a time not looked for. The <ns0:hi>Virgins</ns0:hi> trimming their <ns0:hi>Lamps</ns0:hi> upon the <ns0:hi>cry</ns0:hi> made, signifies the care of Pious Souls, more e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />specially upon any notices of Christs coming, to prepare them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves for the meeting, and Reception of him. The <ns0:hi>foolish Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gins</ns0:hi> late discerning that their Lamps were out, and that they wanted Oyl, lets us know, that Hypocrites and formal Profes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sors, will too late know that Profession without a Root of <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>true Regeneration</ns0:hi> will serve them in no stead. Their ask<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the wise Virgins to lend them some of their Oyl with their refusal, because then they should not have enough for themselves, lets us know the woful shifts that Hypocrites will at last be put to, and how vain their Hopes are, who hope to be relieved, from the <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>good Works</ns0:hi> of others. Their <ns0:hi>going to buy Oyl,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>their being</ns0:hi> shut out before they returned, and <ns0:hi>Knock<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing</ns0:hi> in vain, and in vain crying, <ns0:hi>Lord open</ns0:hi> to us, lets us know, That as the Tree falls so it must lye, That after our buying time in this Life mentioned, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 55.1, 2. is expired: Our State will be determined, that we are concerned to take the Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel of <ns0:hi>Solomon, Eccles.</ns0:hi> 9.10. <ns0:hi>whatsoever thy Hand findeth to do,</ns0:hi> especially for our Souls, <ns0:hi>to do it with thy might, for there is no Work nor Device, nor Knowledge, nor Wisdom in the Grave whither thou goest.</ns0:hi> Therefore we are all concern'd to <ns0:hi>Watch,</ns0:hi> that is, to look that we have not only Lamps, but <ns0:hi>Oyl</ns0:hi> to feed our Lamps, and to keep our Lamps burning, because we know that the <ns0:hi>Bridegroom</ns0:hi> Christ will come, and we do not know at what time he will come, to the General Judgment, or our particular Judgment; for when we dye, we can do no more to make our selves ready for the great coming of Christ to Judge the World, but must appear before him, as we go out of this World. No Oyl after the Determination of our Lives will be to be bought, no further Preparation of our selves is to be made, as our Life leaveth us Judgment will find us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:265" />14 For <ns0:hi>the kingdom of heaven is,</ns0:hi> as a man travel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered to them his goods.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>A Talent is</ns0:hi> 187 <ns0:hi>pound ten Shillings, see on Chap.</ns0:hi> 18.24</ns0:note>15 And unto one he gave five talents, and to a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother two, and to another one, to every man according to his several ability, and straitway took his journey.<ns0:note place="bottom">There is much the same Parable, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 19.12. but the diffe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence is so great in the Narration, and the time and Circumstances, and Scope, seem so different, that the best Expositors think it another, and spoken at another time, tho there be much of this in that: I shall therefore leave the consideration of that in <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> until I meet with it in him, (tho some Interpreters do think this the same with that) and only consider this, as it is before us in this <ns0:hi>Evangelist.</ns0:hi> By the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Heaven,</ns0:hi> is doubtless here to be understood the <ns0:hi>Oeconomy</ns0:hi> of God's Providence in his Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel-Dispensations, the <ns0:hi>Man</ns0:hi> travelling into a far Country, is <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> ascending up to Heaven, who <ns0:hi>when he ascended up on High, gave Gifts unto Men, Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.8. By the <ns0:hi>Goods,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>the Man is</ns0:hi> said to have delivered to his Servants, are to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood the <ns0:hi>Gifts</ns0:hi> which God giveth to Men, being himself (as to his glorious presence, and his principal Residence which is in Heaven at a great distance from us) as a Man in a far Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try, for I see no reason to restrain these Gifts to such as flow from Christ as <ns0:hi>Mediator,</ns0:hi> but rather chuse to interpret it ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerally of all the Gifts of God, whether of <ns0:hi>Providence</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> whereas <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15. it is said that this Man divided his Goods to his Servants <ns0:hi>inequally,</ns0:hi> to one <ns0:hi>Five Talents,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>another two,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>another one,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>every Man according to his several Ability.</ns0:hi> It signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fieth only Gods inequal Distribution of his Gifts to the Sons of Men, according to his own good pleasure, which is true both concerning <ns0:hi>Natural Parts,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Wit, Vnderstanding, Iudgment, Memory,</ns0:hi> as concerning those which the Heathens call good things of <ns0:hi>For<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tune,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Riches, Honours</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Dignities,</ns0:hi> Christians call them the good things of <ns0:hi>Providence,</ns0:hi> under which Notion also come all acquired Habits, or indowments, such as <ns0:hi>Learning, Know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, Moral Habits,</ns0:hi> &c. which tho <ns0:hi>acquired</ns0:hi> are yet <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> because it is the same God <ns0:hi>who gives us Power to get Wealth,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> speaks, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 8.18. who also gives Men <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> to get <ns0:hi>Knowledge,</ns0:hi> and upon Study and Meditation to comprehend the Natures, and Causes of things, and also to Govern, and Bridle our Appetites. Or the Gifts of more <ns0:hi>special Providence,</ns0:hi> or Distin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guishing Grace. I take all those <ns0:hi>Powers</ns0:hi> given to Men, by which they are inabled to do good, or to excell others, to come under the Notion of the <ns0:hi>Goods</ns0:hi> here mentioned, which God Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stributeth inequally according to his own good Pleasure, and as seemeth best <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o his Heavenly Wisdom, for the Government of the Worl<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and the ordering of the affairs of his Church, of all which God wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l have an account one Day, and reward Men ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the Improvement, or no Improvement, which they have made of them in their several Stations.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Then he that ha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                  </ns0:gap> received the five talents, went and traded with the same, and made <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> other five talents.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And likewise he that <ns0:hi>had received</ns0:hi> two, he al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so gained other two.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 But he that had received one, went and digged in the earth, and hid his Lords money.<ns0:note place="bottom">This part in the Parable only sheweth the different use, that Men and Women make of those Gifts, whether of <ns0:hi>Common Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence,</ns0:hi> or of <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> especially <ns0:hi>Common Grace</ns0:hi> which the Lord bestowed on them. Some make a great use of them for the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fit of their Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ter, for the end for which God betrusted them with them, to Wit, the Glory of his holy Name, and the Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of their Souls. Others make no use at all of them for those ends.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 After a long time, the Lord of those servants comes and reckoneth with them.<ns0:note place="bottom">God in the Day of Judgment, will call all Men to account for those Gifts which he hath given them, how they have use<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Days of Li<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e, the Measures of Health, their Knowledge, Wit, Memory, Understanding, their Wealth, Estate, Honours, Dignities, Relations, all their Natural, or acquired Habits, all their Enjoyments, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> for the Honour of his Name, and the advantage of their own Souls.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And so he that had received five talents came, and brought other five talents, saying, Lord thou deliver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />edst unto me five talents, behold I have gained besides them five talents more.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 His Lord, said unto him, Well done thou good and faithful servant, Thou hast been faithful over a few things, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 24.47. Luk. 22.29, 30.</ns0:note> I will make thee ruler over many things, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 He also that had received two talents, came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lents, Behold I have gained two other talents besides them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 His Lord, said unto him, Well done good and faithful servant, Thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.<ns0:note place="bottom">This part of the Parable teacheth us only these things. 1. That some Persons in this World, make a very good use, and Im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />provement of those Gifts, and good things, which God hath be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trusted them with according to the measure with which God hath betrusted them. 2. That those who do so shall in the Day of Judgment have a Liberal reward in the Kingdom of Glory, called here the <ns0:hi>Ioy of their Lord.</ns0:hi> That God doth not expect an Equality of Service from all, but a Service proportionable to those Gifts which God hath given Men, and those shall go to Heaven, who have made a due Improvement of the Gifts, with which God hath blessed them, tho it be not proportionable to the Service which others, of greater parts, and who have had greater ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vantages and opportunities have made; if Men have but two <ns0:hi>Talents</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> yet if they gain other two, they shall go to Heaven at last, as well as those who have had five, and improved them to the gain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of other five. We must take heed of concluding from this part of the Parable, that those who have most given them or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinarily, do make the best Improvement of them, for daily ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perience teacheth us the contrary, neither is the Parable brought to instruct us in any such thing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Then he which had received the one talent came, & said, Lord, I knew thee that thou wert an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thering where thou hast not strawed.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: Lo there thou hast <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> thine.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 His Lord answered, and said unto him, Thou wicked, and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Thou <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, I should have received my own with u<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sury.<ns0:note place="bottom">We must remember that we are in a <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> which (as o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Similitudes) cannot be expected in all things to agree with what it is brought to illustrate. This part of the Parable doth chiefly instruct us in these two things. 1. <ns0:hi>That it is the Genius of wicked Men, to lay the blame of their miscarriages upon others, oft times upon God himself.</ns0:hi> The unprofitable Servant here pretends that the dread of his Lord, as a severe Man, was that which kept him from Labouring, and making an Improvement of the Talent, with which his Master had intrusted him. Thus ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny think that if there be an <ns0:hi>Election <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>f Grace,</ns0:hi> or any thing of special, and <ns0:hi>distinguishing Grace,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Man hath not a perfect Power in his own Will</ns0:hi>; he shall have something to ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cuse himself by before God hereafter, for his not <ns0:hi>Repenting</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>believing</ns0:hi> God in such a Case, condemning Men for un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />belief, and impenitency should reap where he did not sow, and gather where he did not straw. 2. <ns0:hi>Men in their excuses<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which they Fancy in stead of excusing will but accuse<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and Condemn themselves.</ns0:hi> The Lord of the unprofitable Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant tells him, that the Fault lay in his own sloth, and Wicked<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, and his dread of his Lords <ns0:hi>Security,</ns0:hi> was but a meer frivolous Pretence, and unreasonable excuse; for if he had dreaded any such thing, he would have done what he could, he would have put out his Money to the Exchangers, and then he should have received his own with Increase. And shall not God as justly another day, reply upon those who think to excuse their leud and wicked Lives, their impenitency and unbelief, from their not being Elected, not having a Power of themselves to repent and believe, nor peceiving his Efficacious Grace. O you wicked and slothful Wretches! Did you suspect, or Fear you were not Elected? Why then did you not give all Diligence to make your Calling and Election sure? Do you plead the work of Power in your own Wills, to repent and believe, and that I did not give you a special effectual Grace? But had you not a Power to keep from the <ns0:hi>Taverns</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Alehouses?</ns0:hi> To keep from <ns0:hi>Lying,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cursing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Swearing,</ns0:hi> and open Profanation of <ns0:hi>my Sabbaths?</ns0:hi> Had not you a Power, to <ns0:hi>Read,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Hear,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Pray,</ns0:hi> if you had to your utmost used the Talents I gave you, and I had been wanting in my further necessary Influences of Grace, ye might indeed have said something, but when you made no use of the Talents you had, why should I trust you with more? <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> comes by <ns0:hi>Reading, Hearing, Praying,</ns0:hi> you had a Power to these things, these <ns0:hi>Talents</ns0:hi> you had. Why did you not <ns0:hi>Read, Hear, Pray,</ns0:hi> that you might believe? If you took me to be so severe a Master, why did not you do what was in your Power to do, that you might find me otherwise? If you had done, what lay in your Power to do, in the use of those Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lents, which I gave you for that end, you might then have bla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med me if I had not given you more, but you never tryed my kindness in such a Case. So that you are not Ruined by any Severity of mine, but by your own sloth, neglect, and Wicked<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness: Thus much this Parable teacheth us, That God in the recom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pences at the last day of Judgment, will be found just, and sinners will all be found Lyers, and their Damnation will be of themselves.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:266" />28 Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him, which hath ten talents.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 4.25. Luk. 8.18. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 19.26.</ns0:note> For unto every one that hath shall be given, but from him that hath not shall be taken away, even that which he hath.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And cast ye the unprofitable servant into <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.12.</ns0:note> outer darkness, there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">God often in this Life, depriveth Men and Women of those Gifts which he hath given them, and they do not make use of for the Glory of his Name, and the good of their and others Souls, the great ends for which he hath betrusted them with them: But this seems not to be here intended, this Text refer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring to the day of Judgment; all therefore that we are to un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand by this, is, That no Mans Gifts, whether of Nature, or <ns0:hi>Providence,</ns0:hi> of what advantage soever they have been to him in this Life, will be of any Profit to him in the day of Judgment unless he hath in this Life used them, to the ends for which God gave them. In that day he will loose all, and the <ns0:hi>Glory of Heaven,</ns0:hi> shall not be the Port<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>on of them, that have had great <ns0:hi>Talents</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Learning, Wit, Riches, Honours,</ns0:hi> spiritual Gifts, or any thing of that Nature, but of those only, who have used these things to the Honour and Glory of God, and to the advan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tage of their own and others Souls. For all those that have been unprofitable, Hell will be their Portion at last, where their Misery will be, as of those that Live in extreme darkness, continual Weeping, and Gnashing of Teeth. The substance of what is in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29. we met with, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.12. <ns0:hi>To him that hath shall be given,</ns0:hi> &c. But I think, the <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech</ns0:hi> here, is applied differently from the Application of it there. There, <ns0:hi>He that hath,</ns0:hi> seemeth to signifie, He that hath in <ns0:hi>actual Possession</ns0:hi>; for it is said before, <ns0:hi>Because it is given to you, to know the Mysteries of the Kingdom of God.</ns0:hi> So that I take that Text, to contain a Promise of the increase of Grace, to those that have the Seed of God: When as the appearances of it, in others shall not last, but va<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nish away. Here plainly, <ns0:hi>He that hath,</ns0:hi> signifieth, <ns0:hi>He that maketh a good and true use</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>what he hath,</ns0:hi> and thus the Para<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble expounds it. So as the Sense is: He that hath any Talents from God, and maketh use of them, and improveth them for the Honour and Glory of God, shall be rewarded, with further Gifts of Grace, or Glory. But if a Man <ns0:hi>hath not</ns0:hi>; that is, <ns0:hi>Hath,</ns0:hi> but is, as if he had not, making no use of what he hath for the Glory of God: those <ns0:hi>Gifts and Talents</ns0:hi> which he hath, shall be of no Profit and Advantage, but miserable disadvantage to him at last.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zech. 14.5. Chap. 16.27. 1 Thes. 4.16. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ude 14. Rev. 1.7.</ns0:note> When the son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 14.10. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Cor. 5.10.</ns0:note> before him shall be gathered all na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 20.37. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 34.17, 20. Chap. 13.49.</ns0:note> he shall separate them one from ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour having spoken much before of his spiritual King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom, which he exerciseth in his Church, cometh now more plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly to tell the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, what kind of a Kingdom he should further set up, and exercise in the end of the World, far different from that which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> dreamt of, and his own Disciples seemed to have some Expectations of. <ns0:hi>When the Son of Man</ns0:hi>; he who now ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth to you in the form of a Servant, and only as the Son of M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n, <ns0:hi>shall come in his Glory,</ns0:hi> a Glorious manifestation of him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self; he now appeareth, clothed with Flesh, but he shall appear in his Glory, <ns0:hi>and all the Holy Angels with him:</ns0:hi> He shall come with ten thousand of his Saints, <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 14. with <ns0:hi>his mighty An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gels,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Thessal.</ns0:hi> 4.7. <ns0:hi>Then shall he sit</ns0:hi> (after the manner of gerat Princes) upon the <ns0:hi>Throne of his Glory,</ns0:hi> he shall appear in great Splendor, <ns0:hi>And before him shall be gathered all Nations,</ns0:hi> that is, all Persons that ever were, or at that time shall be in the World; the <ns0:hi>Quick</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Dead, Acts</ns0:hi> 10.42. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.1. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.5. He shall send forth his Angels, and say to them, who are his Reapers, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.30. <ns0:hi>Gather together first the Tares, and bind t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>em in Bundles to burn them, but gather the W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>eat into my Barn.</ns0:hi> He by his Angels, shall separate them one from another. as a <ns0:hi>Shepherd,</ns0:hi> who feedeth both Sheep and Goats together, at Night separateth them one from another: So the Saints of God, who are like <ns0:hi>Sheep</ns0:hi> for Whiteness, Gentleness, Innocency, and feed in this World together with <ns0:hi>Stinking</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lascivious Goats,</ns0:hi> the wicked of the World, compared to <ns0:hi>Goats</ns0:hi> for the filthy Qualities by which they resemble them, yet at the day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment Christ shall separate them: <ns0:hi>And he shall set the Sheep a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> his right Hand.</ns0:hi> The right Hand, is the place of Honour and Dignity, and the place for Favourites: Then Christ shall exalt his Saints to great Ho<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>our and Dignity, and shew them his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour; and <ns0:hi>the Goats on the left Hand,</ns0:hi> Wicked men shall rise to <ns0:hi>Shame</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Contempt.</ns0:hi> The right Hand men of the World, shall be at the left Hand of Christ. It shall be then seen, that <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause</ns0:hi> they are People of no understanding, he that formed them, will shew them no Favour.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Then shall the King say to them on his right hand, Come ye blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Mar. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> prepared for you from the foundati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of the world.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The King,</ns0:hi> that is, he who was before called the <ns0:hi>Son of Man,</ns0:hi> who shall then sit <ns0:hi>on the Throne of his Glory.</ns0:hi> He shall say to his Saints, to those on his <ns0:hi>right Hand,</ns0:hi> those whom he designs to Honour, and to Favour, <ns0:hi>Come ye Blessed of my Father:</ns0:hi> You whom my Father hath Blessed with all spiritual Blessings in me, who were also <ns0:hi>Blessed</ns0:hi> in his <ns0:hi>Eternal Thoughts:</ns0:hi> For there was a Kingdom prepared for you, from the Foundation of the World, you have not purchased it by your Works; no it was prepared for you before ever you were, you were Blessed in my Fathers eternal Thoughts, so he prepared a Kingdom for you; and you have been Blessed since with all spiritual Blessings through me, so you are now prepared for it; Therefore, <ns0:hi>Come</ns0:hi> and now <ns0:hi>In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />herit</ns0:hi> it, as that which you are fore-ordained, and born unto, as that which is freely given you, not purchased by you.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 1.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 13.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> I was a stran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger, and ye took me in:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 2 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord when saw we thee an hungred, and fed <ns0:hi>thee</ns0:hi>? or thirsty, and gave <ns0:hi>thee</ns0:hi> drink?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 When saw we thee a stranger, and took <ns0:hi>thee</ns0:hi> in, or naked and clothed <ns0:hi>thee?</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 Or, when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Heb. 6.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Inasmuch as ye have done <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> unto me.<ns0:note place="bottom">The recompences of the last Judgment, are according to the tenour of our good Works, and the desert of evil Works. The King here gives the reason of his Gracious rewarding Sentence: <ns0:hi>For I was an Hungry, and ye fed me.</ns0:hi> This doth not imply any desert, much less any Worthiness of Equality, between the Work and the Reward; but that Evangelical Works, the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ducts of unfeigned Faith and Love, qualifie us by the Covenant of Grace to receive it. The Causes of the Reward are either, the Original Cause; the most free and rich Mercy of God, or the Meritorious, the most perfect Righteousness and Sacrifice of Christ, and the good Works here recited, are infallible signs that the Performers of them are the Objects of the Divine Favour in Predestination, and are truely united to Christ. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides, in the Gospel, which is the Law of Grace, God has Establisht a necessary Connexion, between <ns0:hi>Faith, that works by Love,</ns0:hi> and the Blessed Reward, and acordingly Evangelical words are the Conditi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of our Title, that qualifies us to obtain the Kingdom of Glory, freely promised for Christ's sake to obedient Believers. And in this respect, the dispensing the Reward, may be said to be an Act of Justice, namely in the Faithful performance of the Promise, as in the forgiving sins, which is an Act of pure Mercy; God is said, <ns0:hi>to be Faithful and Iust,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.9. Our Lord here reckons but one <ns0:hi>Species</ns0:hi> of good Works, instead of many, as is usual in Scripture, and he rather chuseth to instance in Works of <ns0:hi>Charity,</ns0:hi> than of <ns0:hi>Piety.</ns0:hi> 1. He knows the hardness of Mens Hearts, and 2. That the Poor, they should have always with them, especially, such as would live Godly, and so be more than others, out of Favour with the World. 3. He knew how acceptable these were to his Father, and had a mind the World should know it, <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 6.8. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 58.7. <ns0:hi>Ezech.</ns0:hi> 18.7. <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.17. And hereby declares, that Acts of Charity to the Souls, makes us fit Subjects for the Divine Mercy in the day of Judgment, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.18. The Answer, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 37. <ns0:hi>Then shall the Righteous answer him, saying,</ns0:hi> &c. only teacheth us this, That at the <ns0:hi>Great day,</ns0:hi> the best of Men shall blush and be asham<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, to h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ar God speak of any good Works they have done, and be swallowed up in the Admiration of Gods Free and infinite Grace, in rewarding any thing which they have done, at so li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beral a Rate. <ns0:hi>And the King shall Answer, and say unto them,</ns0:hi> &c. This only confirmeth what we had, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.42. That Christ looketh upon Acts of kindness done to the meanest Godly Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons, and will reward them, as if they had been done unto himself; so that tho our Charity must not be limited only there, yet it must be chiefly shewn to those of the Houshold of Faith, other Charity may be shewed in Obedience to the Command of God, and have its reward, but none can so Properly be said, to be done to Christ, as that which is done to those, who are his true Members.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:266" />41 Then shall he also say to them on the left hand, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 6.8. Chap. 7.23. Luk. 13.27.</ns0:note> Depart from me ye cursed, into everlast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 For I was an hungry, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred: or a thirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 14.31. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.5. Zech. 2.8.</ns0:note> Inasmuch as ye did <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> not to one of the least of these, ye did <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> not to me.<ns0:note place="bottom">The great King, and Judge of the whole Earth, had before given Sentence for those on his right Hand, who are now possessed of their Kingdom, and sit with him to Judge the World: He now comes to Sentence the Goats at the left Hand, whose Judgment is to <ns0:hi>Eternal Misery</ns0:hi>; lying in two things, in a <ns0:hi>departure from God,</ns0:hi> so as never more to have any Favour from him. 2. In a <ns0:hi>Sense of Pain and Misery,</ns0:hi> exceeding that which Fire causeth to a Body consuming with it. In this Life wicked Men are capable of some Presence of God with them, and receive several Favours from God, in Gifts of <ns0:hi>Common Providence,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Common Grace.</ns0:hi> Which might serve either, as Incouragements to allure them, or means to help them, in turning to God; but having abused these, The righteous God in that day will totally depart from them, and they shall receive no more Tokens of kindness and Favour from him; and whereas, by the advantages they had from such a Presence of Divine Providence, as God was pleased in this Life to allow them, they lived in some degrees of Pleasure and Liberty, which they were not thankful for, they shall at that day be adjudged to <ns0:hi>Eternal Torments.</ns0:hi> Nor shall the Justice of God be impeached, for disproportioning Eternal Torments to Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />porary sinnings; for the infiniteness of the Majesty offended, to which Satisfaction is due, is to be considered, and is so amongst Men, who think it reasonable to recompence a Prince, or Noble Man, for an injury done to them with ten thousand Pounds, which they would not recompence to an Equal, with so many Shillings. Beside, that every Sinner hath sinned, <ns0:hi>in suo infinito,</ns0:hi> to the utmost Line of his time, and wanted nothing, but more time to have sinned more, for he had a Will to have sinned infinitely. This everlasting Fire, is said to be <ns0:hi>prepared for the Devil and his Angels.</ns0:hi> Not because it was not also prepared for Men, but the <ns0:hi>Evil Angels</ns0:hi> were adjudged to it before Man had sinned, so that Man comes but into a share with the <ns0:hi>Evil Angels</ns0:hi>; and by this, God also lets us know, that they are the <ns0:hi>Children of the Devil,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Evil Works, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 8.44. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.8. Having determined their Punishments, and pronounced their Sentence, He comes to justifie himself in it. <ns0:hi>For I was an Hungry, and you gave me no Meat,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>For</ns0:hi> here may be interpreted as a <ns0:hi>Causal,</ns0:hi> for tho none merits his own Salvation; yet every sinners Destruction is of himself, and he meriteth <ns0:hi>his Condemnation.</ns0:hi> The mentioning only of <ns0:hi>sins of Omission,</ns0:hi> and those only, as to <ns0:hi>Acts of Charity,</ns0:hi> doth not only teach us, that sins of <ns0:hi>Omission</ns0:hi> are enough to Damn us, but that Omissi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons of Acts of Charity, to the distressed Members of Christ, are such sins, as if not repented of, and washed off with the Blood of Christ, are enough to Condemn us to the Pit of Hell; and such things as God doth keep in mind, and will in a more special manner reckon with Men for. I cannot pass by a re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flection, which I find almost all Interpreters make upon this Text. If those in the day of Judgment shall be sent to Hell, who do not feed the poor Members of Christ, and give them to drink, when they are Thirsty; what shall be done to them, who pluck the Bread out of their Mouths, which they have got in the Sweat of their Face, and spill the drink, which their own Labours or others Liberality hath given them to drink? If those shall have their Portion with the Devil and his Angels, who give not Entertainment to them when they are banished, and Strangers, what shall become of them who are Instruments of their Banishment, and to make them Strangers? If it shall go so hard with those, that cloth them not when they are Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ked, what shall become of those, who any way help to strip them Naked? If those shall not escape the Vengeance of God, who do not visit them when they are Sick, and in Prison, where shall they appear, who cast them into Prisons, and are means of those Diseases that shorten their Lives, by their barbarous usages of them? Those that smite their fellow-Servants, had need be sure, that it be not for well-doing. Our Lord here tells us, that the <ns0:hi>Wicked</ns0:hi> in that day will say: <ns0:hi>When saw we thee an Hungry,</ns0:hi> &c. They did not deny, that they had refused to give Bread to the Hungry; but they deny that they ever <ns0:hi>saw Christ an Hungry, and did not feed him.</ns0:hi> Persecutors have always ill Names to give the Servants of God, pretending still a great Reverence for God, and Christ. But mark our Lords Answer, and that with an Oath. <ns0:hi>Verily I say unto you, inasmuch as you did it not to one of the least of these, you did it not to me.</ns0:hi> It is no mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter what you thought of, or called those to whom you shewed no Mercy; you see they are here at my <ns0:hi>Right Hand</ns0:hi>; you might have known them to be my <ns0:hi>Sheep,</ns0:hi> you saw them <ns0:hi>Hear</ns0:hi> my <ns0:hi>Voyce,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>following me</ns0:hi>; you in casting them into Prison, ca<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t me, in starving them, you starved me, and in stripping them of their Goods, you stript me. Therefore, <ns0:hi>Go ye Cursed into Everlasting Fire, prepared for the Devil and his Angels.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Dan. 12.2. Joh. 5.29.</ns0:note> these shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life eternal.<ns0:note place="bottom">So then it seems, they shall rise as well as the other, tho they live in the Lands of the <ns0:hi>Grand Seignior,</ns0:hi> or the great <ns0:hi>Mogul,</ns0:hi> they shall not (as some filthy Dreamers have thought) have such a quiet sleep in the Graves, but that the sound of the last Trump shall awaken them. Nor are they out of the Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risdiction of him, that shall be the Judge both of the quick and the dead. Nor shall they escape a Judgment without the Law, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they have sinned without the Law: <ns0:hi>For the invisible things of God, from the Creation of the World are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his Eternal Power and God-head, Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.20. <ns0:hi>they shall perish</ns0:hi> (as they have sinned) <ns0:hi>without the Law, Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.12. They shall go into Everlasting punishment, not a Punishment for a time (as <ns0:hi>Origen</ns0:hi> thought.) But the <ns0:hi>Righteous,</ns0:hi> those who shall be so adjudged, being made so in this Life, by the <ns0:hi>imputed Righteousness of Christ,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Accepted</ns0:hi> as such, for their Holy and sincere Conversation, tho in many things imperfect, shall go into <ns0:hi>Life Eternal,</ns0:hi> which doth not signifie a meer <ns0:hi>Eternal Existence</ns0:hi> (for so the worst of Men shall live Eternally: Or else they could not be capable of Eternal punishment) but an Happy and Blessed Estate, which shall never have an end; and thus <ns0:hi>Eternal Life</ns0:hi> always signifieth in Scripture, being opposed to Eternal Death: Everlasting Fire, the Worm that never dieth, &c. Thus endeth Christ's<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi> of Grace: Or rather, thus shall begin his <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Glory:</ns0:hi> All his Enemies being put under his Feet, and none remaining but this <ns0:hi>Glorious King,</ns0:hi> and those who shall be his true Subjects. Of which Kingdom shall be no end.</ns0:note>
